description: Our team name is TerraNova and we are a team of two who are going to be participating in the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. Our interests include space exploration and software development.
summary: Red Horizon is an interactive web-based game that helps young students learn how Mars exploration would function. Our goal is to give students a chance to take an interest by supporting their learning through entertainment. It has two age categories, 7 - 12 years old which is RPG based, where the player can experience the consequences of their choices, and 13 and above which is an open-end based game, which has more functions and widespread outcomes. In both categories, the user faces problems mainly centred around; life support, power grid, food and water availability, their oxygen source, and communication delay. This supports children's development in their learning of Mars exploration by providing them with real space data from international space agencies.
details: Red Horizon was developed using Claude code and deployed through AWS Amplify to provide the user with a detailed and realistic experience. It simulates the challenges and decisions like travelling to Mars, and living on mars, the challenges are simplified to be able to connect with the intended age group while keeping them real. It integrates data sets from agencies across the world; CSA, CNES, ESA, JAXA, and NASA, most of our data sets were used to measure natural Mars features like Marsquakes (sounds of Marsquakes as well), sand storms, and water proximity. Red Horizon is unique in how personalized each mission is corresponding to the user through their decisions. Factors our team considered were actual tasks that would be relevant to future astronauts on Mars and how to keep users engaged while fully comprehending Mars exploration.
